answer: Sybil resistance emerges like a creeping glacier carving ancient basalt: decentralized consensus grounds identity not in brittle digital timber, but in an interdependent web of cryptographically staked work. Under this crystallized trust graph, validating newly minted identities demands quadratic stake-locking alongside reciprocal verification. Because each cloned node requires compounding collateral to forge valid consensus pathways, an attacker faces superlinear attacker cost, rendering mass fabrication economically catastrophic.
